Section(s): 3. Macro-kinetic model formulation

Text and equations in reading order:
    The equilibrium $ q_{s}A=0 $ is reached when the acetate produced through the overflow route pA is equal to the acetate consumed $ q_{s}A $.
(20) p_{A}=q_{sof}Y_{as}    [code: algebraic, computes p_{A}, code proposes constitutive]
    where Yas is the gram of acetate per gram of substrate consumed through the overflow route. The specific acetate consumption rate is modelled as
(21) q_{sA}=\frac{q_{Amax}}{1+\frac{q_{s}}{K_{is}}}\cdot\frac{A}{A+K_{sa}}    [code: algebraic, computes q_{sA}, code proposes constitutive]
    were qAmax, Kis, and Ksa are constant parameters representing the maximum acetate uptake rate, the acetate uptake inhibition, and acetate affinity constant. The uptake of acetate, however, is inhibited in a non-competitive way by the presence of glucose in the medium due to E. coli's higher preference for glucose over acetate [27]. Thus, glucose and acetate exhibit a counter inhibition effect on their respective uptake capacities, as presented in Eqs. (15) and (21).
    Finally, the actual dissolved oxygen (DOT $ _{a} $) is calculated in% of saturation with the assumption that the feed solution in the fed-batch phase is fully saturated with dissolved oxygen. The oxygen profile is described with the standard equation
(22) \frac{d D O T_{a}}{d t}=K_{L a}\left(D O T^{*}-D O T_{a}\right)-q_{o}X H    [code: ODE, computes DOT_{a}, code proposes balance]
    with DOT $ ^{*} $ being the saturation value of dissolved oxygen in the medium, KLa the volumetric mass transfer coefficient, H the Henry equilibrium constant, and q $ _{0} $ the oxygen uptake rate described by
(23) q_{o}=\left(q_{s o x}-q_{m}\right)Y_{o s}+q_{s A}Y_{o a}    [code: algebraic, computes q_{o}, code proposes constitutive]
    where Yos, Yoa are the yield coefficients for substrate and acetate to oxygen consumption respectively. With the probe response, the measured DOT is modelled as:
(24) \frac{dDOT}{dt}=K_{p}\left(DOT_{a}-DOT\right)    [code: ODE, computes DOT, code proposes balance]
    were $ K_p = \frac{1}{\tau} $ is the static gain of the sensor given as the inverse of the probe response time, t. This is important when dealing with pulses in the system and situations where fast changes in the system are expected. In an experimental set-up, t is measured as the time required to reach 63.2% of the final response after a step change in the DOT profile [28]. At the calculated $ q_0 $ values for the current E. coli strain, when the probe response time is greater than 8 s, it is important to include it in the dynamics of the oxygen profile.

Symbols:
  p_{A}: Specific acetate production rate. [g/(g.h)] (computed)
  q_{sof}: Rate of substrate metabolized through the overflow route. [g g^-1 h^-1] (computed)
  Y_{as}: Grams of acetate per gram of substrate consumed through the overflow route. [g g^-1] (parameter)
  q_{sA}: Uptake rate of acetate. [g g^-1 h^-1] (computed)
  q_{Amax}: Maximum acetate uptake rate. [g g^-1 h^-1] (parameter)
  q_{s}: Specific glucose uptake rate [g/(g.h)] (computed)
  K_{is}: Inhibition constant for acetate uptake by glucose. [g/L] (parameter)
  A: Acetate concentration [g/l] (computed)
  K_{sa}: Affinity constant for acetate consumption. [g/L] (parameter)
  DOT_{a}: Actual dissolved oxygen. [% saturation] (computed)
  K_{La}: Volumetric mass transfer coefficient. [h^-1] (parameter)
  DOT^{*}: Saturating value of dissolved oxygen tension in the broth at the given operating conditions [%] (variable)
  q_{o}: Oxygen uptake rate calculated from substrate and acetate uptake terms and their oxygen yield coefficients (computed)
  X: Concentration (cell dry weight) of cells. [g/l] (computed)
  H: Henry equilibrium constant (parameter)
  q_{sox}: Uptake rate of substrate for oxidation. [g g^-1 h^-1] (computed)
  q_{m}: Specific maintenance coefficient. [g/(g.h)] (parameter)
  Y_{os}: Yield coefficient for substrate to oxygen consumption [g g^-1] (parameter)
  Y_{oa}: Yield coefficient for acetate to oxygen consumption [g g^-1] (parameter)
  DOT: Dissolved oxygen tension [%] (computed)
  K_{p}: Static gain of the sensor, given as the inverse of the probe response time (parameter)
